title: Every libsail read path is timed against a reference that does the same work
body:
Under sail-ce02ff, reading FASTA through `index::Reader` and `FastaParser::parse` took 2 to 6 times as long as needletail. No benchmark covered that path. sufr found the gap when it tried `libsail` in place of needletail.

`benchmarks/src/api.rs` times four of `libsail`'s choices, each against a reference that does the same work:

- `build_index` against a `memchr` floor
- sampling on disk against sampling in memory
- reading records in file order against reading them scattered
- `mmap` against `pread`

Nothing there times the streaming readers or any parser. These paths have no reference today:

| path | reference, a first guess |
|---|---|
| `index::Reader` and `index::Readers` | a `memchr` floor, and needletail for FASTA |
| `lines::Rows` and `lines::line_index` | a `memchr` floor on `\n` |
| `FastaParser::parse` | needletail, and a copy of each line found with `memchr` |
| `StockholmParser::parse` and `HmmParser::parse` | Easel, where an `esl-` miniapp does the same work |
| `HmmerRow`, `HmmerDomRow`, `BlastRow` and `NailRow` | a split on whitespace with `memchr` |
| `IndexedFasta::record` and `try_get` | `pread` of the same byte range |

## Proposal

Add a benchmark for each path to `benchmarks/src/api.rs`, with the reference first, as the file already does. A path slower than its reference by more than the run-to-run spread gets its own bug issue with the numbers.

## Open

- Which reference fits each path.
- The inputs. The widest gap in sail-ce02ff came from long unwrapped records. Each format needs long records and short ones, and wrapped and unwrapped records where the format wraps.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0eeac819
notes.text:
Lessons from sail-ce02ff for choosing each reference:

- Compare a path with a reference that does the same work. needletail's `seq()` borrows a one-line record, so the fair reference for `FastaParser::parse`, which returns an owned record, is needletail with `rec.seq().into_owned()`. Plain needletail looked 1.9x faster on one-line DNA. Owned needletail was 1.15x faster.
- Time `Reader` alone beside the full path. It placed the cost in `parse`, not framing, which the first guesses got wrong.
- Use long one-line records, long wrapped records and many short records. Each one exposed a different cost.
- The harness at `tmp-claude/2026-11-19-fasta-gap/repro` builds against `libsail` by path and is a starting point. It is not committed.
